finding: The live range of $200-$1,125 is about right at the top but looks low at the bottom, and it is wide. We could only build a full parts-plus-labor figure for two of the four classes, because no public source stating a labor time was found for the 2015 Corolla 1.8L or the 2015 BMW 328i N20. Implied totals at $120-$160 per hour: midsize (2016 Camry 2.5L) about $252-$545; truck (2016 F-150 5.0L) about $395-$683. Economy and luxury cannot be totalled; their parts alone run $122-$403 (Corolla) and $224-$737 (328i). The lowest total we can support is about $252 and the lowest benchmark is $350 (AAA), so a $200 floor is below anything found. The $1,125 ceiling matches AAA's $1,100 and is plausible for a European car where the part alone can list at $737, but we could not confirm it with a stated labor time. Our two totals sit below RepairPal ($565-$796) and Kelley Blue Book ($728-$820); the gap is in parts, since our low ends use remanufactured aftermarket units at online prices ($122-$155) while RepairPal's parts figure is $375-$516, and our labor times are do-it-yourself or seller estimates rather than flat-rate book times.
extras: A quote often adds a starting and charging system test or diagnosis fee, a refundable core charge on a remanufactured starter (about $35-$85 on the listings seen), shop supplies, and sales tax. A weak battery or corroded battery cables are often found at the same time and quoted separately. On engines where the starter sits under the intake manifold, new intake gaskets may be added.
